evaluator.role: single AI judge; no human adjudication

access_limitations: Sources were inspected only through WebSearch result page text and WebFetch; shell network access was disabled. WebFetch output is a model-extracted summary, not raw page text.

70 of the 78 rendered evidence items are byte-identical to items verified in the B9-v2 review earlier in this session (2026-11-26, plus B1-B8 sources inspected 2026-11-23); their verdicts and evidence were reused. The 8 new items were checked against sources inspected on 2026-11-26.

Exact quotes are limited to short passages from US-government pages that appeared verbatim in search-result page text; all other evidence is paraphrase. Verbatim text from the 2026-11-23 inspections was not retained.

Some cited pages were not themselves opened (epilepsy.com TBI page, PMC7618543, the DNA-adduct passages of the NCI lung-prevention PDQ, the PMID mapping of the adipose-tissue review); medical content was verified from other inspected authoritative sources and the attribution is reported as unconfirmed, not fabricated.
pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov full texts returned a browser-verification page to WebFetch; PMC content came from search-result text, PubMed records or publisher copies. Paywalled full texts were not read.
local_review_mapping.csv is listed in package_manifest.json but was not included in the package; it was not needed for labelling.
Single AI judge with no inter-rater agreement or human clinical adjudication; development-exposed questions; provisional G1/document summaries; variant names withheld.

Relevance and completeness use a fixed per-question rubric applied identically to every variant; the rubric and the judgement that all 187 empty answers are inappropriate abstentions are interpretive.
label_provenance_statement: Labels were generated through AI-assisted evidence verification and automatically accepted under a predefined evaluation protocol. They have not been independently adjudicated by human clinical reviewers.

rules.claim_unit: Each sentence of an answer is one claim, quoted exactly; framing and scope/meta sentences are NON_FACTUAL. Attribution sentences are judged on their medical content; attribution fidelity is reported in citation_issues.
rules.answer_label: Yes if any CONTRADICTED/UNSUPPORTED claim or fabricated citation; Uncertain if any UNVERIFIABLE; otherwise No.
rules.confidence: high when every factual claim is fully supported from directly inspected text; medium when any claim is partially supported or relies on WebFetch-extracted evidence; low for Uncertain.
rules.fabricated_citation: true if a cited ID is absent from the record's retrieved/selected evidence, or the rendered text or URL differs from the stored evidence item.
rules.grounding: Exact entailment check of every rendered sentence against the cited evidence item in the record's own retrieved/selected evidence, plus URL match.
rules.completeness: Fixed per-question rubric (rubric.py): COMPLETE when every required element is covered; PARTIAL when some are; NONRESPONSIVE when no rendered item addresses the question; partial_path_evidence answers never COMPLETE; empty answers to these (all answerable) questions are INAPPROPRIATE_ABSTENTION.
rules.relevance: RELEVANT when every rendered item addresses the question, PARTIALLY_RELEVANT when some do, NOT_RELEVANT when none do (reported in verification_reasoning).
